Current State — All Commodity / Symbol Combinations

Bullish/Bearish Score: -5 (Very Bearish) to +5 (Very Very Bullish), derived from win-rate × average-return, scaled against the full range observed across all bull and bear deciles for that instrument.

Important: the Decile, N, Win Rate and Win/Loss Ratio columns are backward-looking statistics computed over a fixed historical study period, evaluated against a static, fixed 8-week (40 trading day) holding period for every trade. The Historical Return Trajectory button opens the full forward-path detail for the selected cell on the Return Trajectory tab. Study periods used:

    Minimum sample size: any decile bucket with fewer than 10 historical trades (N < 10) does not have a statistically reliable win rate, return, or drawdown profile computed. In that case the affected stats are shown as "--" rather than a number, and the Bullish/Bearish Score falls back to a fixed mid-tier default (mid-tier bullish in a Bull regime, mid-tier bearish in a Bear regime) rather than a data-driven score. This most often occurs in thinner Bear-regime deciles, where far fewer historical observations exist than in Bull-regime deciles.

    Model Portfolio All-12 · 1‑pick tranche ladder

    A model $100,000 book that, every week, buys the single strongest signal across all 12 symbols (each commodity's 1× and leveraged ETF), ranked by (win-rate × average-return) ÷ |Max 2σ drawdown|, and holds it for a fixed 8 weeks. Eight of these weekly buys overlap at any time — a rolling ladder of eight vintages, each seeded at 1/8 of the book. Weights are left to drift, with one guardrail: if a sleeve ever slips below 5% of the book, it is topped back up to a full 1/8 at its next renewal, funded by trimming the fattest sleeve(s) — never dropping any donor below 1/8. Each week's pick is signaled on the Friday CFTC release and entered at the following Monday's close, so no trade acts on the same session its signal was published. See Page Help for the full logic and metric definitions.

    The grey SPY line inside a tile is $100,000 put into SPY over the same window - buy and hold. Metrics are run through the same math. It appears only where a buy-and-hold comparison is meaningful. Sharpe and Sortino are calendar-annualized (weekly returns compounded to a full year) to match CAGR and the other metrics on this tab, and are computed in excess of a 3.47%/yr risk-free rate (annualized 1–3 month T-bill). No trading costs or slippage are modeled.

    Equity Curve

    Current Holdings

    Symbol% of PortfolioSharesFirst EnteredAverage Entry PriceCurrent PriceP&L %Max DD %MFE %Win

    Holdings are aggregated by symbol (all vintages of the same ETF combined). % of Portfolio is the symbol's share of the book; Shares is the total shares held across those vintages; Average Entry Price is the cost-weighted average across that symbol's vintages; P&L % is current price vs that average; Max DD % and MFE % are the worst peak-to-trough drop and best gain of the net position since its first entry.

    This Week's Actions

    Exactly one vintage rolls per week: the slice that has completed its 8-week hold is sold and its proceeds buy this week's top pick. Sells are listed before buys. If the renewing sleeve had slipped below 5% of the book, a TRIM line appears too — the fattest sleeve is pared back to refill the laggard to a full 1/8 on its new symbol. If this week's pick is the same symbol that's maturing (and no top-up is due), no trade is needed — that vintage simply rolls forward.

    Closed Trades

    SymbolSignal (Fri)Entered (Mon)Sold (Mon)DaysEntryShares% of Book (entry)ExitReturn %Max DD %MFE %WinP&L $

    Every row is one completed 8-week hold, in the exact order the model traded them — each sell funds the next week's buy. Shares and % of Book (entry) show the position's size when it was opened (shares = dollars deployed ÷ entry price; % of book = its weight the week it was entered, normally ~12.5%, higher when it was a top-up). P&L $ is the actual dollars the position realized. A † marks the nine positions that were partially trimmed mid-hold to top up a laggard sleeve, so their P&L reflects the size actually carried rather than a full-size hold.
